text: 5 times better. no matter the dozens of cans of tuna from the supermarket: it’s fuel for an untapped dignity—a splendid sleek energy of YEA especially when it all becomes too much: this over-thought upon the happenings of humans. ∫ In the morning we awakened, man and wife, as so many people do. But there was a new cat, a 5th cat, a very young fellow who had entered our family that night. He was terrorized by life, hungry, lonely. Somehow in our drunkenness, we had fed him. Now, down on the rug, he whirled about, leaped in joy and in some panic of the newness of things, he looked at us with his wild yellow eyes. A good sign: a new life, like ours. Then I thought, today Linda Lee will eat something besides that cheesecake wedding cake (the remainder of which was jammed into the refrigerator). And someday we will see all those many wedding photos and we will live it all over again and ingest, once again, the crazy magic. “Good morning, Mrs. Bukowski,” I said, rather laughing. “Good morning, dear husband,” Linda Lee answered, rather laughing back. And we had this new door in the side of our house. And many more doors to open. ∫ a cat is a cat is a cat is a cat she’s whistling and clapping for the cats at 2 a.m. as I sit in here with my wine and my Beethoven. “they’re just prowling,” I tell her . . . Beethoven rattles his bones in majesty. and those damn cats don’t even care about any of that. and if they did I wouldn’t like them at all: things begin to lose their natural value as they near human endeavor. nothing against Beethoven: he did fine for what he was but I wouldn’t want him on my rug with one leg over his head while he was licking his balls. ∫ another casualty cat got run over now silver screw holding together a broken femur right leg bound in bright red bandage got cat home from vet’s took my eye off him for a moment he ran across floor dragging his red leg chasing the female cat worst thing the fucker could do he’s in the penalty box now sweating it out he’s just like the rest of us he has these large yellow eyes staring only wanting to live the good life. Beauty ∫ my cat, the writer as I sit in front of this machine my cat Ting sits behind me on the back of my chair. now as I type this he steps upon an open drawer and then out across this desk. now his nose is over this paper and he watches me type. then he leaves off goes over and sticks his nose into a coffee cup. now he’s back his head across this piece of paper. he sticks his paw down into the ribbon. I hit a key and he leaps away. now he just sits and watches me type. I’ve moved my wineglass and bottle to the other side of the machine. the radio plays bad piano music. Ting just sits and looks at this typer. do you think he wants to be a writer? or was he one in the past? I dislike cute cat poems but I’ve written one anyhow. now there’s a fly in here and Ting watches his every move. it’s 11:45 p.m. and I’m drunk . . . listen, relax, you’ve read worse poems than this . . . and I’ve written them. ∫ 5 cats cat A: old granny, pointed teeth, she’s seen too much, she doesn’t give a damn about the Russian Revolution or any others; Harry Truman playing the piano with Lauren Bacall plopped thereupon doesn’t matter; she’s mean because to survive is sometimes mean. cat B: a bland fellow, gets along with all the other cats and he likes to sleep against my lower leg at night, left leg while I’m on my back, right leg when I’m on my belly and he’s heard Johnny Carson and maybe has seen him but like me he never laughs at that. cat C: the clown, big boy, huge eyes, he’s tan and white, the favorite of the cat hospital, they think he’s funny but when he goes out at night there are soon horrible screams from the darkness. he’s killed one of the neighbors cats, mutilated another. he returns with tufts of fur sticking out of his mouth, endless scratches, dried blood, swellings, ripped tail, ripped paw, he’s had one broken leg, he’s always back at the hospital, he’s so often bandaged, red and white bandages, he rips them off, we jam antibiotic pills into his mouth and try to keep him in at night. he’s never read Schopenhauer but would dig hell out of him. cat D: the mother of cats B and C. and all the cats chase her except B. cat E does too but I haven’t told you about cat E. stick around. anyhow, cat D gets most of the love from us, her existence is so damned, she just hides and hides and licks her grievous wounds. if she could read she would probably wax to the sisters Brontë. cat E: just came to the door one day, all black, the perfect animal, each movement slides through space without friction, he’s the leopard, those yellow eyes look at you and say: kill or be killed, he is centuries old, the other cats stay away from him, including the great fighter: C. it’s the EYES, they can’t handle those EYES. he will never be tamed yet manage to pick him up, stroke him, put him down, he will follow you for some minutes, purring: he is thanking you for not murdering him. he’d scare hell out of Charles Manson and if he had to choose from such things in a milder moment he might possibly go Celine. anyhow, all these strange hunks
